sources_searched: Europe PMC metadata and full-text XML
query_families: stopping flexibility power and sample size
qualitative reflexivity saturation and data adequacy
data provenance FAIR and analytic reproducibility
inclusion_criteria: empirical or meta-research evidence for a protocol/conduct risk
methods evaluation or framework with a bounded contract implication
current major reporting standard with explicit scope
computational or data-provenance evidence relevant to traceability
exclusion_criteria: journal prestige or citation count alone
tertiary summary when a primary source was available
source whose DOI/title identity could not be reconciled
search_protocol.deduplication_key: DOI when available; otherwise canonical version-of-record URL and title
search_protocol.stopping_rule: stop this iteration after every maintained adapter had multiple relevant sources, every automatic blocker had empirical/methodological support, and additional searches mainly produced domain refinements

sources.title: The Preregistration Revolution
supports: preregistration separates prediction from postdiction
timing relative to outcome access is central to a confirmatory label
limits: preregistration does not by itself guarantee valid design, conduct, analysis, or conclusions
practical accommodations are needed for pre-existing data

sources.title: The Past, Present and Future of Registered Reports
supports: results-blind review can reduce publication and reporting incentives
registered reports bind question and methods before results are known
limits: registered reports are explicitly not a universal solution for irreproducibility
publication model evidence does not impose registration on every study archetype

sources.title: An Excess of Positive Results: Comparing the Standard Psychology Literature With Registered Reports
supports: registered reports in the studied sample had a much lower proportion of positive first-hypothesis results than standard reports
result-contingent publication and analysis can distort the visible evidence base
limits: observational comparison cannot isolate publication bias from every alternative explanation
psychology sample and publication format constrain transfer

sources.title: False-Positive Psychology: Undisclosed Flexibility in Data Collection and Analysis Allows Presenting Anything as Significant
supports: undisclosed analytic and data-collection flexibility can inflate false-positive findings
stopping, exclusions, outcomes, and model choices require prospective specification or transparent disclosure
limits: demonstrations use selected psychology scenarios
disclosure reduces hidden flexibility but does not certify validity

sources.title: A Manifesto for Reproducible Science
supports: blinding, randomization, preregistration, power, reporting, and incentives interact
data-independent confirmatory work must be distinguished from data-contingent exploration
limits: proposals require continuing empirical evaluation
no single reform is sufficient or universally applicable

sources.title: Empirical Evidence for Selective Reporting of Outcomes in Randomized Trials: Comparison of Protocols to Published Articles
supports: primary outcomes were frequently changed, introduced, or omitted between protocols and publications
statistically significant efficacy and harm outcomes were more completely reported
limits: cohort comes from trials approved in one regional ethics system in 1994-1995
protocol comparison detects discrepancies but does not determine every reason or consequence

sources.title: Systematic Review of the Empirical Evidence of Study Publication Bias and Outcome Reporting Bias — An Updated Review
supports: significant results were associated with publication and fuller outcome reporting
protocol-publication inconsistencies and outcome switching require explicit traceability
limits: included studies were heterogeneous and were not meta-analyzed
evidence base centered on randomized trials

sources.title: Empirical Evidence of Bias in Treatment Effect Estimates in Controlled Trials With Different Interventions and Outcomes
supports: inadequate or unclear concealment and lack of blinding were associated with exaggerated effects for subjective outcomes
conduct risks depend on outcome type rather than a universal constant penalty
limits: meta-epidemiological associations vary among meta-analyses
objective and mortality outcomes showed less evidence of the same average bias

sources.title: Influence of Reported Study Design Characteristics on Intervention Effect Estimates From Randomized, Controlled Trials
supports: inadequate sequence generation, concealment, and blinding were associated with average exaggeration and heterogeneity
randomization and blinding execution are evidence-relevant conduct fields
limits: incomplete reporting and confounding among design characteristics limit causal interpretation
average effects were driven mainly by subjective outcomes

sources.title: SPIRIT 2025 Statement: Updated Guideline for Protocols of Randomised Trials
supports: minimum protocol fields for randomized trials
protocol versions, outcomes, harms, data handling, analysis, oversight, and open-science records
limits: a reporting guideline does not prove that planned methods are valid or were executed
scope is randomized-trial protocols

sources.title: CONSORT 2025 Statement: Updated Guideline for Reporting Randomised Trials
supports: trial reports should expose registration, protocol/SAP access, participant flow, outcomes, harms, intervention delivery, and open-science information
reported conduct must be reconciled with planned protocol objects
limits: completeness of reporting is not proof of unbiased conduct or a correct causal claim
scope is randomized-trial reports

sources.title: Better Reporting of Interventions: Template for Intervention Description and Replication (TIDieR) Checklist and Guide
supports: intervention content, provider, mode, setting, dose, tailoring, modification, and actual fidelity must be recoverable
planned delivery and actual delivery are distinct fields
limits: emphasis is reporting and replication, not proof of intervention efficacy
guidance began as a trial extension although intended for evaluative designs more broadly

sources.title: A Conceptual Framework for Implementation Fidelity
supports: fidelity includes adherence in content, frequency, duration, and coverage
quality of delivery, participant responsiveness, facilitation, and complexity can moderate fidelity
limits: framework organizes measurement but does not define one universal fidelity instrument
essential components remain intervention-specific

sources.title: Using Big Data to Emulate a Target Trial When a Randomized Trial Is Not Available
supports: observational causal analyses should specify the target trial and decision-relevant treatment strategies
explicit target-trial components expose design and analysis mismatches
limits: emulation does not remove unmeasured confounding or guarantee identifiability
framework addresses causal comparative-effectiveness questions, not all observational studies

sources.title: Specifying a Target Trial Prevents Immortal Time Bias and Other Self-Inflicted Injuries in Observational Analyses
supports: eligibility, treatment assignment, and time zero must be aligned in observational causal designs
explicit protocol emulation can prevent avoidable immortal-time bias
limits: target-trial specification does not solve residual confounding
not every descriptive or associational study seeks a causal target trial

sources.title: The Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) Statement
supports: observational reports should distinguish what was planned, done, found, and inferred
cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies require design-specific transparency
limits: the authors explicitly state STROBE is not a design prescription or quality-assessment instrument
does not cover every observational design or establish causal validity

sources.title: Leakage and the Reproducibility Crisis in Machine-Learning-Based Science
supports: train/test non-independence and preprocessing on held-out data can create irreproducible performance
scientific ML leakage controls differ from competition and engineering settings
limits: review is a documented lower bound rather than a systematic meta-review
leakage definitions depend on prediction target, unit, time, hierarchy, and intended deployment

sources.title: Improving Reproducibility in Machine Learning Research: A Report From the NeurIPS 2019 Reproducibility Program
supports: computational claims need code, data, hyperparameters, seeds, resources, and result variability records
checklists and artifact workflows can improve record completeness
limits: conference programme evidence does not certify scientific validity or benchmark fairness
machine-learning scope and volunteer artifact access constrain transfer

sources.title: Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research
supports: every result should retain executable or sufficiently detailed workflow provenance
versions, parameters, intermediate results, seeds, and raw data behind plots should be retained
limits: rules are general guidance rather than controlled evidence for every implementation
exact reproducibility can still be limited by hardware, nondeterminism, licensing, or unavailable data

sources.title: Reproducible Research in Computational Science
supports: computational reproducibility can serve as a minimum transparency standard when full replication is unavailable
analysis artifacts must be inspectable to evaluate published computational claims
limits: reproducibility is not independent replication or proof that a claim is correct
perspective does not specify one complete implementation contract

sources.title: Deriving Chemosensitivity From Cell Lines: Forensic Bioinformatics and Reproducible Research in High-Throughput Biology
supports: weak data-processing provenance can conceal simple but consequential indexing and labeling errors
raw-to-result lineage and exact processing records are safety-relevant
limits: case studies are from a specific high-throughput biomedical setting
forensic reconstruction does not estimate the prevalence of errors in all computational science

sources.title: An Empirical Analysis of Journal Policy Effectiveness for Computational Reproducibility
supports: availability-on-request policies yielded limited artifact acquisition and reproduction in the studied sample
claimed availability must be verified by accessible, usable artifacts rather than prose alone
limits: single-journal policy sample and author response affect estimates
reproduction of reported findings is not independent scientific replication

sources.title: Data Availability, Reusability, and Analytic Reproducibility: Evaluating the Impact of a Mandatory Open Data Policy at the Journal Cognition
supports: data availability, data reusability, and analytic reproducibility are distinct states
unclear curation and analysis specification can prevent reproduction despite a sharing policy
limits: observational evaluation at one journal cannot isolate all policy effects
most unreproduced values did not clearly overturn original conclusions

sources.title: Reporting Animal Research: Explanation and Elaboration for the ARRIVE Guidelines 2.0
supports: animal studies should expose design, experimental unit, sample-size reasoning, inclusion/exclusion, randomization, blinding, outcomes, statistics, procedures, and welfare
planned and actual exclusions and experimental units are critical to interpretation
limits: reporting completion does not prove low risk of bias or ethical adequacy
animal species, interventions, and laboratory contexts require domain-specific additions

sources.title: A Call for Transparent Reporting to Optimize the Predictive Value of Preclinical Research
supports: sample-size estimation, randomization, blinding, and data handling are core preclinical rigor records
better reporting can expose whether bias-reduction measures were used
limits: workshop recommendation is not controlled evidence of effect for every field
transparent reporting alone does not ensure the measures were performed correctly

sources.title: Survey of the Quality of Experimental Design, Statistical Analysis and Reporting of Research Using Animals
supports: many surveyed animal studies omitted randomization, blinding, sample-size calculation, and unit clarity
poor design and reporting records obstruct bias assessment and replication
limits: sample covered selected journals and a historical publication period
absence of reporting is not always proof the conduct step was absent, so execution receipts should distinguish unknown from not done

sources.title: Risk of Bias in Reports of In Vivo Research: A Focus for Improvement
supports: randomization and other bias-reduction measures were infrequently reported in sampled in-vivo research
journal prestige is not a substitute for design and conduct evidence
limits: reporting audit cannot always determine what was actually performed
sample and automated/manual extraction choices constrain prevalence estimates

sources.title: Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Protocols (PRISMA-P) 2015 Statement
supports: systematic reviews need explicit protocol question, eligibility, information sources, search, study records, outcomes, bias, and synthesis plans
protocol amendments must remain traceable
limits: reporting protocol items do not guarantee a complete search or valid synthesis
primarily developed for systematic reviews and meta-analyses of health research

sources.title: PRISMA 2020 Explanation and Elaboration: Updated Guidance and Exemplars for Reporting Systematic Reviews
supports: review reports should expose registration/protocol, amendments, searches, selection, extraction, risk of bias, synthesis, certainty, and availability
review conduct should reconcile with the frozen protocol and exact search records
limits: PRISMA is a reporting guideline, not proof that the review is unbiased or exhaustive
extensions may be required for specialized review types

sources.title: PRISMA-S: An Extension to the PRISMA Statement for Reporting Literature Searches in Systematic Reviews
supports: database/platform identities, exact strategies, limits, dates, supplementary search routes, deduplication, and peer review should be recoverable
search strings must be preserved as actually executed
limits: authors state the checklist guides reporting rather than conduct
not every item applies to every review or information source

sources.title: Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ): A 32-Item Checklist for Interviews and Focus Groups
supports: qualitative interview/focus-group reports need research-team reflexivity, study design, analysis, context, recording, theme derivation, and supporting evidence
sampling and respondent validation choices should be explicit
limits: COREQ is specific to interviews and focus groups
checklist completion does not adjudicate paradigm-specific quality or interpretation

sources.title: Standards for Reporting Qualitative Research: A Synthesis of Recommendations
supports: qualitative reporting needs transparent approach, researcher characteristics/reflexivity, context, sampling, data collection, analysis, trustworthiness, and interpretation
standards must preserve methodological and paradigmatic flexibility
limits: SRQR is a reporting synthesis rather than a universal conduct algorithm
broad scope requires study-specific operationalization

sources.title: How Many Interviews Are Enough?
supports: saturation can be operationalized and tracked during thematic analysis
sample-size sufficiency depends on thematic yield and variability rather than a universal interview count
limits: findings came from one relatively homogeneous study and cannot set a universal threshold
early metatheme occurrence is not proof of adequate depth for other questions or analyses

sources.title: Sample Size in Qualitative Interview Studies: Guided by Information Power
supports: qualitative sample adequacy depends on aim, sample specificity, theory, dialogue quality, and analysis strategy
saturation is methodology-dependent and inconsistently applied
limits: information power is a planning framework, not a mechanical stopping formula
does not replace reflexive evaluation of data adequacy during conduct

sources.title: Characterising and Justifying Sample Size Sufficiency in Interview-Based Studies
supports: sample-size justifications in qualitative health research were often absent or weak
data adequacy should be justified from study-specific features rather than community norms alone
limits: sample covers three health-related journals and single-interview-per-participant designs
reporting patterns do not establish a universal sufficient sample size

sources.title: The FAIR Guiding Principles for Scientific Data Management and Stewardship
supports: research objects need findable, accessible under stated conditions, interoperable, reusable metadata and provenance
sensitive data can be discoverable and governed without being openly exposed
limits: FAIR is not identical to open and does not certify data accuracy
authors state the principles precede implementation and are not a single standard or technology

sources.title: Sample Size Justification
supports: sample-size rationale should align informational value with inferential goals
power, precision, resource constraints, population coverage, heuristics, or acknowledged absence are distinct rationales
limits: no one justification applies to every quantitative design
a justified sample size does not guarantee unbiased measurement or analysis

sources.title: A Tutorial on Sensitivity Analyses in Clinical Trials: The What, Why, When and How
supports: sensitivity analyses test robustness to assumptions, models, values, and analytic choices
primary and sensitivity conclusions should be interpreted together
limits: clinical-trial examples do not specify every field-specific robustness analysis
agreement across chosen sensitivities cannot rule out all misspecification

sources.title: A Systematic Scoping Review of Adherence to Reporting Guidelines in Health Care Literature
supports: reporting-guideline adherence was frequently suboptimal across surveyed reviews
endorsement and policy can improve completeness but require implementation
limits: review covers health-care reporting up to 2012
adherence scores do not prove methodological quality or valid conduct

generalization_rule: No reporting standard, registration state, study design, or reproducibility receipt is a universal quality certificate. Apply only evidence-backed obligations matched to the study archetype and preserve transfer limits.

triggers: new meta-research reversing a blocker basis
update_policy.historical_policy: version a new registry; do not rewrite the recorded basis of prior evaluations
